formal-implication.translation: Universal conditional over variables: φ(x) implies ψ(x) for all x
formal-implication.definition: Russell's foundational relation in PoM (1903, §§1, 5–6): an implication holding for every value of one or more variables, by which pure mathematics asserts hypothetical deductions ('if S is a Euclidean space, then P holds of S') without categorical existential commitments.

logical-constant.translation: Indefinable or purely logical primitive notion
logical-constant.definition: In PoM §1 & §10, the sole non-variable constituents permitted in propositions of pure mathematics: implication, class-membership (ε), 'such that', relation, and truth.

propositional-function.translation: Open expression φ(x) yielding a proposition for each value of x
propositional-function.definition: An expression containing one or more real variables which becomes a determinate true or false proposition whenever definite terms are substituted for its variables.

projective-geometry.translation: Qualitative geometry of incidence, collineation, and harmonic separation
projective-geometry.definition: The geometry of properties invariant under central projection and section, requiring neither betweenness on open lines nor quantitative distance; axiomatized qualitatively via incidence and von Staudt's quadrilateral construction (EFG Ch. III Sec. A; PoM Ch. XLV).

descriptive-geometry.translation: Geometry of open serial order and betweenness (Pasch–Peano)
descriptive-geometry.definition: In Russell's 1903 classification (PoM Ch. XLVI, §§374–387), the study of spaces where two points determine an open serial segment (betweenness) rather than a closed projective line—applicable to Euclidean and hyperbolic spaces prior to introducing metrical congruence, and completed into projective space via ideal elements.

metrical-geometry.translation: Quantitative geometry of distance, congruence, angle, area, and volume
metrical-geometry.definition: The branch of geometry introducing quantitative equality (congruence) of stretches, distances, and angles, presupposing projective or descriptive order (EFG Ch. III Sec. B; PoM Ch. XLVII).

harmonic-range.translation: Four collinear points (A, B, C, D) in harmonic conjugation
harmonic-range.definition: Four collinear points such that A and C are harmonic conjugates with respect to B and D: metrically having cross-ratio -1, and projectively defined without metrics by von Staudt's complete quadrilateral construction (EFG §113; PoM §365).

quadrilateral-construction.translation: Von Staudt's pure-incidence construction of the harmonic fourth point
quadrilateral-construction.definition: Given collinear points A, B, D, constructing the unique harmonic conjugate C of A with respect to B, D by projecting from an external point O and intersecting diagonals of a complete quadrilateral—uniqueness in a plane following from three-dimensional incidence via Desargues's theorem (EFG §113; PoM §365).

anharmonic-ratio.translation: Projective invariant of four collinear points or concurrent rays
anharmonic-ratio.definition: The double ratio (AB/CB) / (AD/CD) preserved under perspective projection; in pure projective geometry, assigned numerically via Möbius nets and Dedekind continuity without appeal to metrical distance (EFG §§111–112; PoM §370).

involution.translation: Symmetric projective pairing of collinear points with double points
involution.definition: A projective correspondence on a line that interchanges conjugate pairs; hyperbolic involutions possess two real double points harmonic with every conjugate pair, whereas elliptic involutions have none (PoM §366).

moebius-net.translation: Countable dense harmonic net on a projective line or plane
moebius-net.definition: The denumerable progression of points generated from three initial collinear points (0, 1, ∞) by repeated harmonic quadrilateral constructions, establishing rational projective coordinates and projective order (PoM §368).

duality.translation: Reciprocity of points and planes in 3-space (or points and lines in 2-space)
duality.definition: The formal symmetry of projective axioms under uniform interchange of 'point' and 'plane' (leaving 'straight line' invariant in three dimensions), doubling every projective theorem (EFG §107; PoM §373).

betweenness.translation: Triadic open-order relation of collinear points
betweenness.definition: The primitive order relation axiomatized by Pasch, Peano, and Hilbert, analyzed by Russell in PoM Part IV and Ch. XLVI as generated by transitive asymmetrical serial relations along a line.

separation-of-couples.translation: Tetradic cyclic order relation on a closed series (ab // cd)
separation-of-couples.definition: Vailati's five-axiom symmetrical transitive relation between point-pairs (a, c) and (b, d) on a closed projective or elliptic line where simple triadic betweenness fails because any two points bound two complementary segments (PoM §§194, 367, 398).

ideal-elements.headword: ideal elements (points, lines, and planes at infinity)
ideal-elements.translation: Logical classes (sheaves/pencils) completing a descriptive space into a projective space
ideal-elements.definition: Following Pasch, an 'ideal point' is defined logically—without postulating fictitious entities—as an entire bundle (sheaf) of lines meeting pairwise in planes, allowing parallel or ultra-parallel lines to share an ideal intersection (PoM §§383–386).

superposition.translation: Geometric proof of congruence by transporting one figure onto another
superposition.definition: Euclid's method in I.4, I.8, and C.N. 4; rejected by Russell in PoM §390 as logically circular because spatial points are immobile positions while moving material bodies presupposes an antecedent metrical definition of rigidity; rehabilitated epistemologically by Hoenen via extension as materia intelligibilis.

stretch.translation: Open or closed segment of points between two endpoints on a line
stretch.definition: The class of intermediate terms (or the generating serial relation restricted to them) between two collinear points A and B, contrasted by Russell with 'distance', which is an indivisible two-term relation (PoM §§169–170, 393–398).

magnitude-of-divisibility.translation: Quantitative measure of a stretch, area, or volume as a property of serial relations
magnitude-of-divisibility.definition: Russell's relational interpretation of extensive spatial quantity (PoM §§162, 396–397): since all continuous stretches have the same Cantor cardinality 2^α₀, length belongs not to the point-set itself but to equivalence classes of generating serial relations.

the-absolute.translation: Invariant conic or quadric locus defining a Cayley–Klein projective metric
the-absolute.definition: Cayley and Klein's fixed second-degree locus in projective space relative to which distance and angle are logarithmic functions of cross-ratios: an imaginary quadric yields elliptic geometry, a real non-degenerate quadric yields hyperbolic geometry, and a degenerate imaginary conic in a plane yields Euclidean geometry (EFG §31; PoM §§407–409).

metageometry.translation: General / non-Euclidean geometry investigating axiom independence
metageometry.definition: Term used throughout Russell's 1897 Essay for the synthetic (Gauss, Lobachevsky, Bolyai), metrical-differential (Riemann, Helmholtz, Beltrami), and projective (Cayley, Klein, Lie) generalizations of Euclidean geometry.

manifold.translation: Continuous or discrete n-tuply extended system of determinations
manifold.definition: Riemann's general class-concept of multiply extended magnitudes (1854), critiqued in EFG Ch. II (§§60–65) for neglecting qualitative relational order and reformulated logically in PoM Ch. XLIV as a multi-dimensional series.

measure-of-curvature.translation: Intrinsic Gaussian / Riemannian curvature constant k
measure-of-curvature.definition: Intrinsic parameter characterizing homogeneous spaces admitting free mobility: k = 0 for Euclidean space, k < 0 for Lobachevskian (hyperbolic) space, and k > 0 for spherical and elliptic spaces (EFG §§20–23).

free-mobility.translation: Invariance of spatial magnitudes under continuous change of position
free-mobility.definition: In EFG (§§146–154), the a priori metrical postulate that spatial magnitudes are independent of place, equivalent to constant Riemannian curvature and homogeneity of space.

form-of-externality.translation: Relational condition of experiencing simultaneous substantival diversity
form-of-externality.definition: Central philosophical concept of Russell's 1897 Essay (Chs. III–IV): any intuitive relational medium rendering experience of diverse interrelated things possible—from which Russell deduced projective geometry and free mobility as a priori before abandoning transcendental arguments in 1903.

materia-intelligibilis.definition: Aristotle's and Aquinas's designation (ὕλη νοητή) for continuous extension abstracted from sensible qualities, invoked by Hoenen (Caput IV & VII) as the principle of individuation and congruence answering Russell's attack on Euclid I.4.

motion-geometric.translation: Class of metric-preserving one-one point transformations
motion-geometric.definition: In PoM §§390 & 395, Russell's static relational replacement for kinematic transport: a group of bijective point-correlations leaving all distances and metrical properties invariant (axiomatized directly as an indefinable by Pieri, 1899).

point-spatial.translation: Simple unextended term of spatial relations
point-spatial.definition: Treated in EFG (§§117, 189–204) as infected with a dialectical contradiction between unextended simplicity and spatiality, then vindicated in PoM (Ch. LI, §§423–431) as a logically consistent substantive term of multi-dimensional serial relations.
